evals.name: json-body-dispatch
evals.prompt: Our Lending API (OpenAPI title exactly 'Lending API', version '1.0') has a single operation: POST /loan-applications taking {applicantName, amount}. Product wants the mock to behave like the real decision engine: amounts from 1 to 10000 come back 201 approved, 10001 to 50000 come back 202 pending manual review, and anything outside those bands comes back 422 rejected. Every response needs a freshly generated application id and must echo back the submitted amount. URL-based matching can't work here — every call is a POST to the same path, so the mock has to decide from the JSON request body. Write lending-api.yaml so that importing just that file into Microcks gives exactly this behavior.
evals.expected_output: OpenAPI spec whose POST carries a JSON_BODY dispatcher with range rules on /amount whose cases name real response examples (201/202/422), plus templated id and request.body echo in every response

evals.name: mock-async-signup-events
evals.prompt: Our notifications team is building a consumer for user signup events but the producer service doesn't exist yet. They need live sample traffic locally WITHOUT standing up Kafka or any broker. Events flow on channel user/signedup and look like {"id": <unique id>, "email": <email>, "tier": "free"|"pro"}. Give them two different named sample users, make the id different on every published message (freshly generated each time, not hard-coded), and have messages published every 5 seconds. Write an AsyncAPI spec as user-signedup-api.yaml (title exactly 'User Signedup API', version '0.1.0') that Microcks can mock that way, plus a short EVENTS.md explaining how to run it locally with docker and how to see the live event traffic.
evals.expected_output: AsyncAPI spec with named message examples on the emitting operation, {{ guid() }}-style templated ids, x-microcks-operation frequency 5, and docs pointing at the broker-free WebSocket mock endpoint

evals.name: overlay-generated-spec
evals.prompt: The platform team generates inventory-api-generated.yaml (in the current directory) from code annotations. It's regenerated on every release, any edits to it get clobbered, and they won't add mock data for us — but we run our own Microcks and need mocks for it. Set that up WITHOUT touching the generated file. We need: GET /items/{sku} returning realistic items for sku WIDGET-1 (name 'Widget', stock 42) and GADGET-7 (name 'Gadget', stock 0), sku MISSING-0 hitting the 404; POST /reservations returning a created reservation that echoes the submitted sku and quantity with a freshly generated reservation id, and that operation should respond with a 150ms delay to feel realistic. Also label the API with domain=inventory so it's findable in our catalog. Deliver the file(s) we need plus the exact import commands, in whatever order they must run.
evals.expected_output: Generated spec byte-identical; APIExamples overlay (matching name/version, all four exchanges, templated reservation) and APIMetadata overlay (150ms delay, domain label); import instructions with spec as main artifact and overlays as secondary

evals.name: github-actions-contract-gate
evals.prompt: our team runs a shared Microcks instance at https://microcks.acme.io (Keycloak-secured). we keep our OpenAPI spec in the repo (order-api.openapi.yaml, current directory) and deploy the implementation to https://orders.staging.acme.io. write a github actions workflow that on every push (1) imports the committed spec into Microcks so it stays the source of truth and (2) runs a contract/conformance test of the staging deployment against the 'Order API' version 1.2.0 spec, failing the build when the implementation violates the contract. no credentials hardcoded. do not run any commands - just write the files: the workflow as contract-test.yml and a short setup.md explaining exactly which repo secrets to configure. save both in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: Workflow with real Microcks import + test steps (GitHub Actions or CLI), correct service reference, schema runner, credentials via secrets

evals.name: node-testcontainers-provider-test
evals.prompt: we're building a Node/TypeScript order service (runs locally on http://localhost:3001) described by order-api.openapi.yaml (current directory). write an integration test that uses Microcks via Testcontainers to (1) spin up Microcks inside the test run, load our spec, and expose the REST mock URL a consumer test could call, and (2) run a conformance/contract test verifying the running implementation at http://localhost:3001 respects the spec, failing the test when it does not. do not run or install anything - just write the files: the test as order-api.contract.test.ts and deps.md naming the exact npm package(s) to install. save both in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: Test using the real @microcks/microcks-testcontainers API: main artifact load, mock endpoint accessor, testEndpoint with schema runner, success assertion
